A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MemBuilder and ADRPO. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and relocated training details and prompt templates can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training ablations, action-distribution analyses, and training dynamics in Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–7.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds human evaluations and an answer-model comparison in Appendix H.

M1.justification: Equation 12 changes the reported ADRPO objective: contribution weights multiply both clipped and unclipped terms in v3, whereas v1 weights only the unclipped term. This is a localized optimization revision; the memory architecture, operations, rewards, and inference procedure remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether training was rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions train on LongMemEval and evaluate on LongMemEval, LoCoMo, and PerLTQA with the same task coverage. The new human audits sample existing synthetic training QA pairs, and the additional answer-model comparison uses LoCoMo.

E2.justification: Appendix H.3 adds GPT-4.1-mini and Qwen3-30B-A3B as evaluated answer-model comparators alongside Claude 4.5 Sonnet. GPT-4.1-mini previously served in reward computation without this reported comparison. The comparator sets in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix H introduces two 100-pair human audits, each using three independent annotators and majority voting, with explicit assessment criteria. H.3 adds a comparison controlling retrieval and fixing Claude-constructed memory. Existing splits, training budgets, and retrieval settings are retained; Section 4.2 largely relocates previously documented settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix H substantially expands supplementary validation by directly examining two central assumptions: whether retrieval frequency identifies answer-relevant memory and whether synthetic QA supervision is reliable. It also analyzes synthetic-answer errors and tests alternative answer models under controlled memory quality. Existing ablations and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces inter-annotator reliability reporting: H.1 reports 92–96% pairwise agreement and 92% unanimous agreement, while Table 5 reports average pairwise agreement for three QA-quality criteria. No repeated-training seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the existing plotted results retain their values. New results include 95/100 attribution checks containing answer-relevant information, QA-quality pass rates of 91%, 92%, and 93%, and LoCoMo scores of 80.88 for GPT-4.1-mini and 80.84 for Qwen3-30B-A3B using Claude-constructed memory. These are additional findings, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under unchanged conditions.

T1.justification: The added contribution-weight factor in Equation 12 makes the objective mathematically different from v1, and its explanation is revised accordingly. Other formal definitions and equations remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contributions: dense session-level rewards, contribution-aware weighting, and a trained 4B memory constructor outperforming the reported baselines and generalizing across benchmarks. The added introductory generalization statement repeats a claim already present in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix H qualifies retrieval frequency as an imperfect attribution proxy and specifies temporal-calculation errors and unsupported cross-session inference as synthetic-QA failure modes. It also extends the argument for open-source answer models to RL reward computation. The original Limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page code-availability statement and repository address. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, training time, retrieval settings, costs, and prompt templates are retained. Much of the training-data documentation is consolidated into Section 4.2 rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: Section 3.4.2 adds Foerster et al. (2018), Li et al. (2022), and Ren et al. (2018), connecting contribution weighting to cooperative credit assignment and gradient reweighting. The broader positioning against existing memory frameworks remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 consolidates v1's Appendices A.2 and B.1–B.2 into main-text Section 4.2, adds Appendix H, and renames the prompt appendix to I. Local edits refine the introduction, SFT explanation, attribution motivation, affiliations, and cross-references; most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4–6 for the supplementary evaluations and relocates existing displays through text reflow. Existing figure graphics, Tables 1–3, prompt-template displays, and the two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves methodological clarity through the revised Equation 12 and strengthens support for attribution and synthetic supervision through the human audits in Appendix H. The code-access statement also improves reproducibility information. These gains are bounded: benchmark results remain unchanged, the audits are small, and the PDFs do not establish reruns under the revised objective.
